blocks.text: The Zscaler service uses the Advanced Threats Protection policy to protect your traffic from fraud, unauthorized communication, and other malicious objects and scripts. The Zscaler service identifies malicious scripts and applications on both hacked and legitimate websites and prevents them from downloading to the end user's browser by using a combination of methods to detect various phishing techniques, including signature-based and AI/ML models and to protect against URL-based phishing techniques, such as typosquatting, punycode, character substitution, domain hijacking, and many more.

If you have Advanced Threat Protection as well as IPS Control, any rules you create for Advanced Threat Protection are evaluated first. To learn how this policy fits into the overall order of policy enforcement, see About Policy Enforcement.
Advanced Threat Protection policies provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Identify and prevent malicious scripts and applications on both hacked and legitimate websites.
Protect your traffic from fraud, unauthorized communication, attacks, and malicious behaviors.

blocks.heading: About the Advanced Threat Protection Policy Page

blocks.text: On the Advanced Threat Protection Policy page (Policies > Cybersecurity > Internet & SaaS > Advanced Threat Protection), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View the recommended Advanced Threat Protection Policy.
Set the Suspicious Content Protection (Page Risk) slider to the page risk tolerance score of your organization.
Configure the Malicious Active Content Protection section.
Configure the Unauthorized Communication Protection section.
Configure the Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Protection section.
Configure the Suspicious Destinations Protection section.
Configure the P2P File Sharing Protection section.
Configure the P2P Anonymizer Protection section.
Configure the P2P VoIP Protection section.
